definition: Policy gradient methods are a class of reinforcement learning algorithms and a sub-class of policy optimization methods.
details: Unlike value-based methods which learn a value function to derive a policy, policy optimization methods directly learn a policy function π {\displaystyle \pi } that selects actions without consulting a value function. For policy gradient to apply, the policy function π θ {\displaystyle \pi _{\theta }} is parameterized by a differentiable parameter θ {\displaystyle \theta } .

explainer.lead: Policy gradient methods are a class of reinforcement learning algorithms that directly learn a policy selecting actions, without consulting a value function. They are a sub-class of policy optimization methods.

tiers.eli5: Instead of scoring every possible move first, the agent practices the moves themselves and nudges toward the ones that paid off.
tiers.practitioner: Used where actions are continuous or stochastic and value-based methods struggle. A pitfall is high variance in gradient estimates, which usually needs baselines or many samples.
tiers.paperLevel: For the method to apply, the policy pi_theta must be parameterized by a differentiable theta, and learning adjusts theta directly from the policy. Because it optimizes the policy without a value function, estimates can carry high variance.

explainer.example: A robot arm policy parameterized by a neural network is updated directly from trial outcomes to favor actions that scored higher reward.
